intro_messages.speaker: Deoran
intro_messages.message: Here we are. Ethiliel has returned to the Aethenwood, Urza Afalas has fled into the night, and it comes to us to deal with whatever lies below. We must find the source of the undead and destroy it.
intro_messages.message_fr: Nous y voilà. Ethiliel est retournée à la forêt d'Aethen, Urza Afalas a fui dans la nuit, et il nous revient de faire face à ce qui se cache ci-dessous. Nous devons trouver la source des morts-vivants et la détruire.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Look out, a troll! Stay back everyone, it might leave us alone if we keep our distance.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Who you? You dead one? I smash dead ones!
Mmm... no, dead ones do not speak. You humans. Humanses long time no see.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Humanses... I remember humanses. Humans go squish, fun to smash! What you doing in caves?

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Err, no need for any squishing, we don’t mean to trespass on your territory. We’re hunting the undead and have no quarrel with you.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Deads! Nasty deads take our home, make us hide! I hates them! They too stupid to find us here, but we no leave here either.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: It seems that we have a common enemy, then. Would you like to join forces to defeat the undead? My soldiers aren’t well-suited to fighting in caves.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Join? Join with humanses? Hmm. Okay. Humans friends. No squish friends.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: We help you beat deads, but after they gone we take back our home and you leave. Okay?

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: It’s a deal.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Who comes... My old tormentors?

a.message_mari: Gods... that skull, those eyes. I had almost hoped the lady was right, but now... even in the Estmarks I never thought I’d live to lay eyes on an lich.
a.message_gerrick: Dear Haldric! I had almost hoped the lady was right, but now... Whatever that elf used to be in life, in death it’s become something far, far worse.
a.message_hylas: Light protect us. I had almost hoped the lady was right, but now... Here lies the source of the spreading corruption: a lich most foul.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: I am Deoran, soldier of the South Guard! We have come to put an end to your villainy, Mebrin of the elves — if that is who you are.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Mebrin? No, I am called Mal M’Brin now, mortals. It is the name I took when I unchained myself from the shallow-mindedness of my kind and passed over into enlightenment.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: There is infinity at the brink of death... I have touched the void at the heart of all things, and I have begun to probe the mystic arts far beyond what any living elf knows.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message_mari: You’ve gone mad! Whatever you once were, you are nothing but evil now! Once Captain Mari and I defeat you, these lands will finally be safe.
a.message_gerrick: You’ve gone mad! Whatever you once were, you are nothing but evil now! Once Sir Gerrick and I defeat you, these lands will finally be safe.
a.message_hylas: You’ve gone mad! Whatever you once were, you are nothing but evil now! Once Minister Hylas and I defeat you, these lands will finally be safe.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I just made a ranged attack! I had to stand right next to this Quintain (yes, this is different from how most games handle ranged attacks), but because the dummy has no ranged weapon of its own it was unable to retaliate.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I just made a ranged attack! I had to stand right next to this $second_unit.language_name (yes, this is different from how most games handle ranged attacks), but because the $second_unit.language_name has no ranged weapon of its own it was unable to retaliate.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I just made a ranged attack! I had to stand right next to this $second_unit.language_name (yes, this is different from how most games handle ranged attacks), but because the $second_unit.language_name has no ranged weapon of his own he was unable to retaliate.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I missed all $consecutive_misses strikes! I tried my best, but this enemy had a high chance to evade. I might have had better odds attacking a different enemy.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: A good commander understands the odds, and knows how to both exploit good luck and mitigate bad luck. After all, both good and bad luck are equally likely!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I got lucky and hit all $consecutive_hits strikes! Good luck will sometimes happen, but a good commander knows how to win without relying on it. After all, bad luck happens just as often as good luck!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I missed all $consecutive_misses strikes, even though my enemy had a low chance to evade! That’s unlucky, but bad luck happens just as often as good luck — a good commander knows how to plan around both!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I hit all $consecutive_hits strikes, even though my enemy had a high chance to evade! Luck works both ways — sometimes I miss strikes when I was likely to hit, but sometimes I also hit strikes that I was likely to miss — like now!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Ah ha, ha ha ha ha. I am no stranger to pain, Deoran of the humans.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: You think yourself wise, to have followed me down into these dark depths? You have only sown the seeds of your own destruction!

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: What the— it’s a cave-in!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Accursed humans, you fools will never leave this place. While you frittered away your final days, Ethiliel has already begun to avenge me.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: I felt her emotions, felt her intentions, fed her intentions... You and I may both perish today, but my revenge has already begun...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have failed my kingdom and duty...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Yeah... I should’ve figured I wouldn’t get a happy ending...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have given all in service of my kingdom...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: May the Light guide you where I have failed...

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I have lost everything helping the humans... Now they will surely perish!

a.speaker: unit
a.message: I perish! Such wasted potential! I’d gained much experience, and was close to becoming something more...

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: One of your high-experience units has died! Take care to protect your experienced soldiers, so that they can eventually advance to powerful Level 2 veterans.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Argh, I fall! All my hard-won battle experience is lost! I will not be easy to replace, Deoran...

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: One of your high-level veterans has died! Take care to protect your promoted soldiers, so that you can recall them in future battles.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Pathetic. Ethiliel I would respect, but you? Humans are not worth my time to slay. Pursue me if you dare.

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Ethiliel spoke so highly of you, but you truly have gone mad. Would that we had listened to Urza Afalas from the beginning!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Mad? I am furious!! You accursed mudlings took me and tormented me, tortured me for sport! I knew that once the first strand of black magic left my hands, there would be no turning back. But I would suffer this humiliation no longer...

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: I taught the summoning of powers beyond the control of your feeble kin, powers that fed upon your race’s filth and greed. Content with only meagre tricks, you mayflies never even noticed as I slowly brought you under my thrall! The Urza brothers sought to enslave me, but it is they who became my slaves in the end.

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: I do not fear oblivion. There can be no horrors worse than that to which I have already been subjected. Even if taking vengeance on your race requires me to destroy myself, it will be worth the sacrifice!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: For if I was wise before, I have now become omniscient! The race of man shall be stricken off the face of the green world. Your corpses will serve me! Your bones will dance for my pleasure! I’ll make humanity into the mindless slaves that you all deserve to be!

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: What the— it’s a cave-in!

a.speaker: Mebrin
a.message: Accursed humans, you fools will never leave this place. Even if taking vengeance on your race requires me to destroy myself, it will be well worth the sacrifice!

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: You have run out of turns to complete the scenario, and have been defeated!

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: They’ve broken through the trapdoor and entered the refugee cellar! Even if we could still manage to win by force of arms, Westin is doomed without its people...

a.speaker: Deoran
a.message: Taste cold steel!

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: One of your units has reached max XP, and has advanced a level! It is now significantly more powerful, and has been fully healed! For a full description of what one of your units can do, right-click it and select “Unit Type Description.”
My healing magic is potent, but I cannot use it to heal myself. I’ll have to spend some time in a village to recover.

a.speaker: unit
a.message: Our bows and spears are nearly useless against these skeletons! They have nothing for our shafts to pierce but air!

a.speaker: narrator
a.message: To see what damage resistances and vulnerabilities a unit has, right-click it and select “Unit Type Description.”
